title: Sensitivity & Uncertainty
pickFieldDesc: Pick a field to analyse how its scenario-derived environmental features respond to the executed transformation parameters.
mainDesc: Deterministic one-factor-at-a-time analysis and optional joint parameter grids over an immutable scenario execution. The explored parameter-range envelope is a deterministic sensitivity result — not a confidence or probability interval. No yield, climate or rainfall predictions exist here.
noFinalizedScenarios: No finalized scenarios for this field yet — create one in the Scenarios tab.
noCompletedExecutions: No completed executions for this scenario — execute it in the Scenarios tab first.
reproductionDesc: The analysis first reproduced the source execution exactly before comparing anything. A failed reproduction aborts the analysis — no substitute baseline.
notAnalysedDesc: Inherited verbatim from the source execution — reported, never fabricated.
defineDesc: Bounds are user-supplied assumptions for a deterministic experiment — they contain the source execution's reference values and imply no probability distribution.
reasonNotConfigured: parameter not configured in the source execution; no reference value exists
includeGridLabel: Also evaluate the joint deterministic parameter grid (both axes reuse these bounds)
oatDesc: Each parameter varies over the explored bounds while every other configured parameter is held at its reference value. Slopes keep their units and are never compared across different units.
showingFirstResponses: Showing the first {shown} of {total} responses — narrow with the classification filter or a specific feature to see more.
noGrid: No joint parameter grid was requested for this analysis.
interactionContrastHint: finite-grid interaction contrast — not a Sobol index
showingFirstSummaries: Showing the first {shown} of {total} grid summaries — per-feature detail is available through the API's feature_code filter.
verifyDesc: Recomputes the analysis checksum from persisted artifacts and re-checks the source-run pins. Confirms the integrity of a hypothetical analysis — never that transformed values are observations.
